primary_antecedent.author: Lars Hörmander
primary_antecedent.title: The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators III: Pseudo-Differential Operators
primary_antecedent.edition: Springer 2007, reprint of the corrected 1994 edition
primary_antecedent.locator: Sections 18.3 and 24.7; the fixed admissible source tests and smooth coefficient-parameter estimate in Propositions 24.7.1 and 24.7.1-prime, printed pages 465–467.
primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Independent constructive domination of a smooth residual parameter family by one compact residual test using exact tangential output packing; combination with a fixed elliptic tester gives a fixed source pair in positive boundary dimension.

source_correspondence: S0 states positive tangential dimension, smooth parameter dependence in every full residual or symbol seminorm, common compact supports and uniform off-cone bounds after parameter derivatives. The result has two fixed source tests.

S1 uses a finite parameter partition, compact cutoffs and smooth periodic extension inside an already available open parameter neighborhood. Constant families use a dummy circle; parameter-boundary extension is not invented.

S2 integrates the entire resolved kernel. Periodic integration by parts gives arbitrary polynomial decay in every residual seminorm. Product-torus uniqueness is proved from circle completeness by induction and Fubini. The lattice enumeration transfers the decay to a single integer index.

S3 gives exact disjoint tangential cubes with centers 1/(j+1), radii 1/[10(j+1)^2], and the sharp uniform consecutive ratio bound 13/60. The square-root Jacobian gives actual L2 isometries; normal and input coordinates stay fixed.

S4 applies output relocation only to residual kernels. The full normalized kernel retains every density and normal-ratio factor. Derivative growth is polynomial in the packing index and is absorbed by Fourier decay. The sum converges with all resolved derivatives and side weights, including zero jets at the accumulation point.

S5 proves exact orthogonality of the packed outputs and the full infinite sum-of-squares norm identity. Cauchy–Schwarz and a direct integral bound on the weights dominate the entire parameter family by the one actual residual source norm.
S6 treats finite operator families, finite parameter charts and finite vector outputs through one combined enumeration. The scalar construction still has scalar output.

S7 retains the exact fixed elliptic parametrix remainder. Uniform separated-product estimates after every parameter derivative make the remainder a smooth residual family. Properness gives fixed compact input and output supports, and the order-zero factor gives the actual L2 bound.

S8 applies the construction to the finite normal-recovery source tree, whose parameter derivatives keep the same order and cone support. One fixed order-minus-two test and one fixed residual test give the actual H2 graph, equation and both traces. The source may vary with the coefficient parameter.
The fixed graph completion uses the earlier flat-transpose uniqueness argument and the bounded map into the original finite tree graph. It does not infer graph density from density in B.

S9 retains the positive-dimensional boundary restriction and both actual fixed tests. Single-scalar tester assembly, the zero-dimensional boundary case where needed, uniform other regimes and the full observation theorem remain active.

Three full solutions check all interval and Jacobian factors, give a sharp two-mode equality example and disprove residual domination for a family that is only individually residual. The last argument includes the original kernel behavior at the output boundary.

The original figure depicts the first six exact tangential output intervals and the exact two-mode norm weights. Ten desktop captures, the whole figure and two mobile samples were inspected. Twenty-six exact checks, 152 formulas and 25 displays assist the full analytic review.

Fourteen proof entries bind to 1885 earlier entries in 101 maps, including 92 external Lebl proofs. Approved source credit is retained. Internal export P514 closure and full-course completion are not claimed.
